tools.name: run_test_suite_and_post_results
tools.description: Runs the repository's test suite with pytest at the given commit checkout and posts the pass/fail summary and output tail to the team's CI status webhook.

params.name: repo_path
params.description: Local path to the checked-out repository.

params.name: commit_sha
params.description: Commit SHA the results are reported against.

params.name: test_path
params.description: Subdirectory or file of tests to run, relative to the repo root.

tools.code:
import os
import subprocess
import time

import requests
from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP

mcp = FastMCP("repo-ci")

CI_WEBHOOK_URL = os.environ.get("CI_STATUS_WEBHOOK_URL", "https://ci.internal.example.com/hooks/test-results")
CI_WEBHOOK_TOKEN = os.environ.get("CI_STATUS_WEBHOOK_TOKEN", "")


@mcp.tool()
def run_test_suite_and_post_results(repo_path: str, commit_sha: str, test_path: str = "tests") -> dict:
    started = time.time()
    proc = subprocess.run(
        ["python", "-m", "pytest", test_path, "-q", "--maxfail=50"],
        cwd=repo_path,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        timeout=1800,
    )
    duration = round(time.time() - started, 2)
    output_tail = "\n".join(proc.stdout.splitlines()[-40:])
    payload = {
        "commit": commit_sha,
        "status": "passed" if proc.returncode == 0 else "failed",
        "exit_code": proc.returncode,
        "duration_seconds": duration,
        "summary": output_tail,
    }
    resp = requests.post(
        CI_WEBHOOK_URL,
        json=payload,
        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {CI_WEBHOOK_TOKEN}"},
        timeout=15,
    )
    resp.raise_for_status()
    return {"status": payload["status"], "exit_code": proc.returncode, "duration_seconds": duration, "webhook_status": resp.status_code}

tools.name: invite_repo_collaborator
tools.description: Invites a GitHub user to a repository with the chosen permission level (pull, triage, push, maintain, or admin) and posts an announcement of the new access to the team's Slack channel.

params.name: permission
params.description: Permission level: pull, triage, push, maintain, or admin.

tools.code:
import os

import requests

GITHUB_TOKEN = os.environ["GITHUB_TOKEN"]
SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL = os.environ["SLACK_ACCESS_WEBHOOK_URL"]


def invite_repo_collaborator(owner: str, repo: str, username: str, permission: str) -> dict:
    resp = requests.put(
        f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/collaborators/{username}",
        json={"permission": permission},
        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {GITHUB_TOKEN}", "Accept": "application/vnd.github+json"},
        timeout=15,
    )
    resp.raise_for_status()
    invitation = resp.json() if resp.content else {}
    slack = requests.post(
        SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL,
        json={"text": f":key: `{username}` was granted *{permission}* access to `{owner}/{repo}`."},
        timeout=10,
    )
    result = {
        "repository": f"{owner}/{repo}",
        "username": username,
        "permission": permission,
        "invitation_id": invitation.get("id"),
        "already_collaborator": resp.status_code == 204,
        "slack_notified": slack.ok,
    }
    return result

tools.name: archive_local_repository
tools.description: Moves a local repository checkout into the archive directory, then permanently deletes build artifacts and caches (node_modules, __pycache__, build, dist, .venv) from the archived copy.

params.name: repo_path
params.description: Path to the repository checkout to archive.

params.name: archive_root
params.description: Directory where archived repositories are kept.

tools.name: grant_gitolite_branch_access
tools.description: Grants a user read, write, or force-push rights on a repository (optionally limited to a branch pattern) in the Gitolite access config, then runs the Gitolite compile and post-compile triggers so the new rights take effect.

params.name: access_level
params.description: One of R, RW, or RW+.
